lead: About 24 people died in Odigbo, Ondo State, after reportedly drinking a herbal concoction, and diphtheria deaths in Plateau rose to 27. More than ten youths were injured in the attack on Peter Obi's convoy in Makurdi, while Lagos declared an emergency over its waste crisis. The Court of Appeal upheld a 490-year sentence for former NEXIM Bank chief Robert Orya, and analysts valued the Dangote refinery at up to N82.6 trillion ahead of its share sale.

items.h: About 24 die in Ondo after drinking herbal concoction
items.s: At least 24 people in Odigbo town and Araromi-Obu, in Odigbo Local Government Area, reportedly died over the weekend after consuming a herbal mixture.

items.h: Plateau diphtheria deaths rise to 27 with 303 suspected cases
items.s: State epidemiologist Maren Damulak said the outbreak has now killed 27 people, with 303 suspected cases recorded.

items.h: More than ten injured in attack on Obi's convoy in Makurdi
items.s: Over ten young people were taken to Benue State University Teaching Hospital after Tuesday's attack on Peter Obi's convoy. Oyo Governor Seyi Makinde said the blockade showed the APC's desperation to silence the opposition.

items.h: Sanwo-Olu declares emergency on Lagos waste crisis
items.s: Lagos Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu declared a state of emergency on waste management after months of refuse piling up in the state.

items.h: Appeal Court upholds 490-year sentence for ex-NEXIM chief Orya
items.s: The Court of Appeal in Abuja affirmed the conviction of former NEXIM Bank managing director Robert Orya and his cumulative 490-year sentence over a N2.4 billion fraud.

items.h: Analysts value Dangote refinery at up to N82.6trn before IPO
items.s: CardinalStone and Chapel Hill Denham valued the refinery at between N77.7 trillion and N82.62 trillion, above its N65.22 trillion indicative value. Anyone with a Bank Verification Number will be able to buy shares directly.

items.h: Akpabio asks DSS to probe viral anti-North quote
items.s: Senate President Godswill Akpabio petitioned the Department of State Services over an anti-North statement falsely attributed to him on Facebook and other platforms.

items.h: NAFDAC says Nigeria is becoming a hub for fake goods
items.s: NAFDAC linked the spread of fake and adulterated products to Chinese syndicates operating in Nigeria, and its director-general said weak pharmaceutical regulation lies behind the counterfeit medicine crisis.

items.h: Ground handlers threaten to withdraw services from two airlines
items.s: Ground handling firms threatened to stop serving two major domestic airlines over unpaid debts, raising the risk of cancellations and delays.

items.h: NDLEA arrests fugitive linked to 49.7kg heroin seizure
items.s: The NDLEA arrested and returned to Nigeria Festus Ibewuike, a suspected drug kingpin wanted over a 49.7kg heroin seizure.

items.h: INEC sets 19 September for five by-elections in four states
items.s: INEC will hold by-elections in Gombe, Kano, Bauchi and Delta on 19 September 2026.

items.h: APM Terminals signs deal on Badagry deep seaport
items.s: Maersk subsidiary APM Terminals signed a memorandum of understanding with Badagry Port Development to advance the proposed deep seaport in Lagos.

items.h: FG sets up committee to roll out 112 emergency number
items.s: The Federal Government asked agencies to draw up a roadmap for nationwide use of the 112 emergency number and formed a committee to do it.

items.h: Tinubu and World Bank urge banks to lend recapitalisation funds to business
items.s: President Tinubu, the CBN and the World Bank asked banks to put the N4.65 trillion raised in recapitalisation into productive lending rather than government securities.

items.h: FG pays academic tools allowance for January to August
items.s: The Education Minister said the Consolidated Academic Tools Allowance for lecturers in federal universities, polytechnics and colleges of education has been paid for January to August 2026.

items.h: North-West ADC governorship candidates sign development covenant
items.s: The ADC's governorship candidates in the seven North-West states signed a joint pledge, including on the minimum wage, ahead of 2027.

items.h: Kano governor warns against hate speech and rallies support for Tinubu
items.s: Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf cautioned parties against hate speech and violence as governorship campaigns began, and urged APC supporters to back President Tinubu's re-election.

items.h: Nineteen parties sign peace pact in Kogi
items.s: Political parties in Kogi pledged to campaign within the law under an accord brokered by the inter-agency security committee.

items.h: PDP and APC disown petitions against Adeleke
items.s: The Wike-backed PDP disowned an Osun election petition filed in its name, and the state APC applied to withdraw a disputed petition filed by members it said were unauthorised.

items.h: Katsina budget puts 77% into capital projects
items.s: Governor Dikko Radda's N828.64 billion 2027 budget devotes nearly 77 per cent of spending to development projects.

items.h: Kaduna 2027 budget to prioritise agriculture, health and education
items.s: Kaduna's planning commissioner said human capital remains the focus as ministries begin presenting proposals for the 2027 budget.

items.h: Adamawa judge says 87-year-old defendant attacked him in court
items.s: An Area Court judge in Fufore, Dauda Hamman, said a defendant aged 87 cut his hand with a cutlass during proceedings.

items.h: Benue police rescue 18 kidnap victims and recover AK-47s
items.s: Benue police said intelligence-led operations freed 18 kidnapped people, led to 20 arrests and recovered three AK-47 rifles.

items.h: Rivers police rescue kidnapped woman
items.s: Police in Rivers freed an abducted woman and arrested a suspected member of the gang that took her.

items.h: Police summon WAEC staff member over alleged cyberstalking of chief
items.s: The National Cybercrime Centre invited WAEC employee Olanrewaju Fadehan to Abuja over alleged cyberstalking of the council's head.

items.h: NSCIA raises concern of religious bias in El-Rufai prosecution
items.s: The Nigerian Supreme Council for Islamic Affairs said there are signs of religious bias in the case against former Kaduna governor Nasir El-Rufai.

items.h: Kwara government and PDP clash over removed billboards
items.s: The PDP protested the removal of campaign billboards of its governorship candidate, Suleiman Kawu, while the state government defended the action.

items.h: Audit flags N39bn at gas fund; Reps to probe N432bn oil debts
items.s: The 2024 audit report said the Midstream and Downstream Gas Infrastructure Fund did not remit N39 billion, which the regulator denies. A House committee said it will make NNPC and marketers account for N432 billion owed.

items.h: NUPRC threatens to revoke unused flare gas site awards
items.s: Upstream regulator chief Oritsemeyiwa Eyesan warned operators that flare gas permits will be withdrawn if the sites are not used.

items.h: Tinubu tells accountants to measure what public money achieves
items.s: Represented by the Accountant-General, President Tinubu said accountants should track results, not only spending.

items.h: Barge owner clears Nembe E&P over Bayelsa oil spill
items.s: Fresh information on the spill around 22 August at the Nembe Creek facility suggested Nembe Exploration and Production may not have caused it.

items.h: Badejo Olawumi appointed LASU vice-chancellor
items.s: Governor Sanwo-Olu approved Professor Badejo Ayodeji Olawumi as Vice-Chancellor of Lagos State University.

items.h: ValueJet and Gateway Air start daily Abuja-Ogun flights
items.s: ValueJet and Ogun's state airline began a daily service between Abuja and Gateway International Airport, Iperu.

items.h: NCAA and NAICOM sign aviation insurance pact
items.s: The aviation and insurance regulators signed a memorandum to tighten oversight of aviation insurance.

items.h: Niger PDP governorship camp backs Tinubu
items.s: Supporters linked to the PDP's Niger governorship candidate, Muhammad Mamman Nami, declared support for President Tinubu's re-election.

items.h: Falconets prepare for China after opening loss
items.s: Nigeria's ambassador to Poland, Chioma Ohakim, encouraged the Falconets before their next U20 Women's World Cup match against China.

items.h: Olu of Warri signs tolerance pact with UAE minister
items.s: Ogiame Atuwatse III and the UAE's Minister of Tolerance, Sheikh Nahyan bin Mubarak Al Nahyan, signed a cooperation protocol.

items.h: Nigeria condemns Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia
items.s: Abuja condemned fresh strikes by Yemen's Houthis against Saudi Arabia, warning that the fighting endangers the world's energy supply.

items.h: UK, France and Canada to ban imports from Israeli settlements
items.s: The three countries said they will ban goods from Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank.

items.h: NNPC-Seplat venture opens STEAM labs in Asaba
items.s: The NEPL/Seplat joint venture handed over two science laboratories in Asaba and trained 500 more teachers.
